To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) aerobic biomineralization rates of atrazine decreased with soil depth in a clay-rich soil, 2) anaerobic biodegradation rates of atrazine in a clay-rich agricultural soil were below the detection limit and 3) aerobic biominerlaization rates of atrizane decreased and anaerobic mineralization increased with soil depth in an agricultural soil with a sandy loam texture.
the rate of mineralization of atrazine decreased with depth in the soil profile at both sites.
the aerobic biomineralization rate constant of atrazine declined and half-lives increased significantly with depth at the site on soybean-corne rotation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biogeochemical fate of the herbicide atrazine in the environment.
the fate of atrazine in agricultural soils and the role of biomineralization.
biogeochemical processes of atrazine and their impact on soil quality in agricultural soils in the Midwestern United States.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
atrazine mineralization is not a simple process in agricultural soils, and it is site specific and influenced by the soil properties and agronomic practices.
aerobic mineralization is more rapid than anaerobic mineralization and the rate constants and half-lives for aerobic mineralization are higher than those for anaerobic mineralizaton.

the fate of atrazine in agricultural soils is complex and depends on many factors including the type of soil, its physical and chemical characteristics, its history of atrazine applications, the type of crops, the depth and time of sampling, and the presence or absence of oxygen and nitrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
atrazine mineralization is not a simple function of soil organic matter or clay fraction, and the mineralization rates are highly variable among sites and depths.
the mineralization rate constants for aerobic biomineralization were 2.4-5.4x10-5 h-1 for surface soils, 0.5-1.4x10 -5 h-1 at 10 cm depth, and 0.2-0.4x10 5 h-1 in subsurface soils (20 cm).
the mineralization of atrazine is not only a function of soil properties and environmental conditions but also the history of the soil and the management practices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
biomineralization rates of atrazine can vary considerably with depth and between different agricultural sites.
atrazine mineralization is site specific.
the kinetic parameters of biomineralization in surface and sub-surface agricultural soils can be very variable and cannot be extrapolate from one site to another.
